metadata.title: TIMSS 2011 Mathematics Framework; TIMSS 2011 Science Framework; TIMSS 2011 Contextual Framework; TIMSS 2011 Assessment Design

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a framework and assessment-design description for TIMSS 2011 rather than an empirical analysis of student microdata. It explains the matrix-sampling approach (14 student achievement booklets with common item blocks) and the use of item-response theory scaling to place responses on common mathematics and science scales. Because no analytic dataset, sampling weights, or replicate-weight procedures are applied in this text, student and replicate weights are not specified. For any downstream empirical use of TIMSS 2011 microdata, analysts should apply the TIMSS complex survey design weights provided in the international database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the clustered sampling of students within schools/classrooms.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this is not an empirical study predicting or scaling student outcomes from microdata; it is an assessment framework describing content domains, cognitive domains, and the matrix-sampling/scaling approach. Missing-data handling is not reported because no analytic sample is constructed and no missingness strategy (e.g., deletion or imputation) is implemented in this document.

data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 2011 is designed to measure mathematics and science achievement at fourth and eighth grades using written tests plus background questionnaires for students, teachers, and school principals. The assessment uses a matrix-sampling approach: the full item pool is packaged into 14 student achievement booklets, with each student completing one booklet, and each item appearing in two booklets to support linking across booklets. Achievement is placed on common mathematics and science scales using item-response theory scaling, enabling trend comparisons across cycles. The framework specifies content domains (e.g., number, algebra, geometry, data and chance; life/physical/earth science; biology/chemistry/physics/earth science) and cognitive domains (knowing, applying, reasoning). Testing time is constrained to 72 minutes (plus a 30-minute questionnaire) at fourth grade and 90 minutes (plus 30 minutes) at eighth grade, with item blocks administered in two parts per booklet.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to TIMSS 2011 assessment frameworks and design documentation, not an empirical predictive/causal paper. As a result, there is no reported student-level analytic sample, no model training or evaluation, no performance metrics, and no explicit survey-weight or missing-data handling strategy implemented in the text. The document’s purpose is to define what TIMSS measures and how the assessment is administered and scaled, so ML-specific fields are intentionally left empty.
